items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1972-09-13
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] They said you played with Johnny Sincere, but he played, you mean in the same band? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, in the same band.

ctx.x: I had a practice. A fellow by the name of Wallace. Wallace gave me that banjo. A five string banjo. And I started to play it and I bought me a book. And I started to play in it. And the fellow knocked on my door and said, Hey man, I need a banjo player for tonight. I said, I don't play no banjo. He said, Oh yeah, you do. I said, I don't. So, he said, Let me see that banjo you got. I said, I showed it to him. He said, Man, come on and play. Make this little change. So, after I played him, I went to World Islands…
They said you played with Johnny Sincere, but he played, you mean in the same band?

Yeah, in the same band. I had a plan with it on the Airline Highway. It was all by the name of Joe, who was in the nightclub. In the 49, I'll never forget. On the 4900 Airline Highway. He used to go down there every Friday and Saturday.

items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1959-09-24
items.q: I got some lessons from him

ctx.x: Now, on the banjo you said Johnny Sincere.
Well, Johnny Sincere on the guitar, yeah. First, you know, I got some lessons from him, because I liked it and I used to worry life out of him to show him some chords, you know what I mean?
I got a whole outfit there, no, no. Did that on the guitar?

items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1959-09-24
items.q: We played at Oakshire's Place out there with Johnny Sensei and myself.

ctx.x: So that's how we played down there. We played at Oakshire's Place out there with Johnny Sensei and myself. Johnny had an old truck he used to call Caledonia. Yeah, I remember him. So, and now, he said, I know, he said, I'm gonna beat you all the time. And when we looked again, we couldn't see Johnny. Johnny was gone. He was living up there in Jefferson somewhere. Way up in Nettenberg Street. Yeah. Had a little house set back in the yard. Yeah, that's, I can't think of a lot of those guys.
Can you remember any other early guitar players that you heard downtown? There was one fellow I never did hear anything about, Richard Payne.
